newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house suspends civil service vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house suspends civil service vote.

text.p: Brazil's lower house suspended a vote on a government civil service reform bill which it hopes will reduce public sector spending on pay and pensions, an official said.
Deputy Michel Temer, lower house president, called off the vote at the request of government whips without giving a reason for his decision.
Deputy Inocencio Oliveira, chief whip of the government-allied Liberal Front Party, said the government would try to vote on the bill April 8.

Earlier the government had said it had reached an agreement with a group of lawmakers who were opposed to the reform bill, principally because a proposed ceiling on pay and pensions would have hurt their income.

Under the agreement the deputies had been due to vote in favor of the reform bill Wednesday in return for government support for an amendment which was to have been put to vote next week and which would have effectively doubled the 10,800 reais ($10,188) monthly ceiling on pay and pensions.

The government chief whip to the lower house Benito Gama said the vote had been postponed after raucous behavior on the floor of the lower house by left wing opposition parties, which he called "verbal abuse" of Temer.
"We are going to vote, we have the votes we need. But this is a complicated vote and it must be done democratically," Gama said.

However a deputy close to the government who asked not to be identified said the decision to call off the vote had been taken amid concerns the government did not have enough votes to reach the three-fifths required as a constitutional amendment.

He said the group of deputies who lobbied for a less rigorous pay and pensions ceiling feared the government would not back their amendment in next week's vote and had withdrawn their support for the vote on the floor.
